events.title: Telegram
events.text:
⚡🇮🇷🇸🇦🇶🇦🇴🇲🇦🇪 Oil exports from Middle Eastern countries have reached their peak since the start of the war in Iran.
Thanks to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, supply volumes have increased to more than 80% of the average daily volume that existed before the war began. The key factor here is adaptation to current conditions: supply volumes are still limited compared to normal levels, but the corridor is functioning well enough to ensure the transportation of a significant portion of the region's crude oil exports.
For the market, this means a partial normalization of physical trade flows through the Persian Gulf and reduces the immediate risk of serious disruptions to exports from one of the world's most important oil transportation hubs. If supply volumes exceed 80% of the pre-war level, then the scenario of the most severe supply shortage becomes less likely, even if logistics remain more complex and vulnerable than before.
The signal is clear: the situation in Hormuz has not yet returned to normal, but the market is being reminded that oil export systems in the Persian Gulf can restore significant volumes faster than the most pessimistic forecasts suggest.

As US forces were about to withdraw from remaining bases in Iraq, Iran’s IRGC took its war message straight to the American public.
👉 Ahead of the looming midterm elections in the US, it argues in an open letter that months of war have failed to deliver the victory Trump repeatedly promised.
“Wake up” and “wrest control back from corrupt politicians,” the letter published by Iranian media urges.
💬 "Although American politicians often win your votes through deception and false promises, as Trump did, you can change the makeup of the government,” it says.
The IRGC argues that the US didn’t achieve any of its declared objectives:
🔴 Iran’s nuclear program was not eliminated, despite thousands of bombs and missiles being used against the country
🔴 The Strait of Hormuz remains under its control
🔴 war has driven up fuel costs, adding pressure to Americans already struggling with inflation
That argument comes as a September Reuters/Ipsos poll found just 34% of Americans approved of the strikes on Iran, while only 17% approved of Trump's handling of the cost of living.

🇮🇱Israeli defense minister threatens Hamas amid reports that Netanyahu ignored pre-October 7 warnings
Israel Katz has claimed in a video statement that Hamas leaders abroad who were involved in the October 7, 2023, attack would be hunted down.
“None of these despicable murderers, who played a central role in the October 7 massacre, may be allowed to die peacefully,” he said.
Katz’s statement came on the heels of a report that Izz al-Din al-Bik, a commander in Hamas’s Northern Gaza Brigade, was killed in an overnight [Israeli airstrike in Gaza City](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75345?single).
The minister’s video address also comes as reports emerge that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [ignored warnings](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75322) from Arab officials of an imminent threat from Gaza in the days leading up to Hamas’s October 7, 2023, attack. One such warning was delivered by United Arab Emirates President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, according to The Washington Post.
